target: Route fresh-16 (free search, round 16): fs16:positive, fs16:assure, fs16:bias, fs16:gate, fs16:contract, fs16:cross, fs16:lip, fs16:noamp, fs16:noqual, fs16:mixmin/mixmono, fs16:topctrl, fs16:two — CORRECTNESS audit

findings.defect: def:fs16-context's ADMISSIBILITY ("stopping when every call is read as a controlled vertex") forbids any nonempty U with some successor in U at every call, i.e. it forbids every directed cycle through call/controlled vertices: an admissible all-call context is exactly an ACYCLIC automaton. So the class the two impossibility theorems quantify over excludes every cyclic finite-state device — which is precisely what the theorem's own consequence sentence claims to cover ("every finite-automaton verdict on a stream of independent plays, H being the automaton, one call per state"), what next_steps 6 tells the project never to re-attempt ("gambler's-ruin counters"), and what supplies EVERY number in rem:fs16-measured. Two consequences: (a) the consequence sentence inside thm:fs16-noamp is not established by the argument given; (b) rem:fs16-measured's "the bound is tight up to a factor of about 8" and the JSON's "the measurements show the linear law is tight, not an artefact of the proof" are statements about a class strictly larger than the hypothesis, and are false for the class actually covered.
findings.evidence: My ctx.admissible, written from def:fs16-context, returns False for the birth-and-death context at s=2,3,4,7,15 (True only at s=1): U={c_1..c_s} has some successor in U at every c_j. The route's own champion 4-state automaton tr=[(1,2),(3,0),(0,4),(5,1)] has the closed set U={0,1,3}. My independent exhaustive search over canonical s-state automata (t_auto.py, dual-number differentiation, nothing taken from the route's two hand-derived systems) reproduces the route's maxima exactly — 1, 4/3, 2, 12/5 at s=1..4 with the same champion and f(1/2)=2/5 — but restricted to ADMISSIBLE contexts the maxima are 1, 1, 5/4, 3/2. A 40000-trial hill-climb over admissible contexts, s<=9 (steep.log): 5257 evaluated points, zero bound violations, worst |dV/dp|/bound = 1/4, steepest |dV/dp|(1/2) found = 5/4; the admissible time-expanded ruin (t_dag.py) has ratio-to-bound 0.250, 0.125, 0.067, 0.042, 0.029, 0.022 at s=1,9,25,49,81,121 — i.e. inside the hypothesis the linear law is NOT tight. REPAIR (verified): replace admissibility by CHANCE-ADMISSIBILITY (only U with both successors in U at every average AND call vertex and some successor at every controlled vertex is empty; equivalently H^{1/2,1/2} is stopping). Then H^{p,q} is stopping for all p,q in (0,1), which is all cor:fs16-lip and thm:fs16-noamp use (delta<=1/4 keeps the interval inside [1/4,3/4]), and both theorems instantiate lem:fs16-gate only at the controlled-vertex-free C_theta: t_repair.py built 1893 compositions H<C_theta> with inadmissible-but-chance-admissible H — all stopping, all values equal to val_{H^{theta,theta}}. Strong admissibility must stay in lem:fs16-gate itself: H = the 2-state ruin context, G = the one-vertex Max game (p=1,q=0) makes H<G> a deterministic 2-cycle, hence non-stopping; 141 of 241 sampled inadmissible compositions were non-stopping (t_inadm.py), although the value identity still held in all of them.

findings.defect: The "In particular p -> V(p,p) is (4/3)(s+3)-Lipschitz on [1/4,3/4]" does not follow from the two displayed bounds: each partial is bounded by ((s+3)/2)/(2p(1-p)) <= (4/3)(s+3) on that interval, and the diagonal derivative is the SUM of the two, giving only (8/3)(s+3). The constant 3/(8 delta) of thm:fs16-noamp is exactly this constant, so the gap propagates. The stated constant is nevertheless TRUE, by a different one-line argument the proof does not give: on the diagonal the gate's two actions coincide, so V(p,p) is the value of a single-parameter chance game and d/dp V(p,p) = sum over ALL calls of N_c Delta_c, one application of eq:fs16-cross.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic: 2p(1-p) >= 3/8 on [1/4,3/4], so ((s+3)/2)(8/3) = (4/3)(s+3) per partial, 2x that for the sum. The statement itself survives: in 500 (context,p) samples the exact diagonal derivative (dual numbers, dp=dq) never exceeded (4/3)(s+3) (worst ratio 0.200), and on the ruin contexts it equals (s+1)/2 exactly at s=1,3,5,7,9,13,15,21 versus the bound s+3.

findings.defect: GAP: the proof says "G/M is stopping for the same reason as in Lem fs16-gate", but the reason there was the ADMISSIBILITY HYPOTHESIS on the context H, and thm:fs16-contract has no such hypothesis — that G/M is stopping has to be derived from G being stopping, and a gate with p_e or q_e in {0,1} is a controlled vertex with a one-point action, so the trap condition for G/M is not inherited from G's by inspection. Missing statement, exactly: "If G is stopping and M has at most the two exits o1,o0, then G/M is stopping." (It is true and provable in three lines: expand a trap of G/M by replacing each gate g_e in it with the set of M-vertices reachable from e under a positional pair witnessing that gate's chosen action; all exits of that set lie in the trap, so the union is a nonempty trap of G.)
findings.evidence: 1751 random contractions rebuilt from the statement (t_contract.py, seeds 91,92,1001,1002; 506 of them with more than one entry) — every value outside M and every gate value matched brute-force w*, and G/M was stopping in every single one, so the assertion is true but unargued.

findings.defect: "polynomial-time equivalent ... by a reduction making a single oracle call and adding six vertices" is not established: when val_G(p) = val_G(q) both m_p and m_q attain the maximum, and an oracle that returns ONE controlled vertex of maximum value leaves the caller unable to decide val_G(p) >= val_G(q) (returning m_q only says val_G(q) >= val_G(p)). The proof dismisses this as "the harmless tie" without argument, but SSG-Compare is exactly the decision the reduction must make. The equivalence survives after a repair the paper should state: damp z_q by an extra epsilon = 2^{-2a-3} (a chain of O(a) average vertices, lem:dyadic-row), which breaks every tie because two distinct values differ by more than 2^{-2a} (lem:payoff-transfer(d)); the reduction then adds O(a) vertices, not six.
findings.evidence: t_top.py rebuilt the reduction: 692 reductions on random stopping SSGs, val_H(v)=val_G(v)/4, val_H(m_p)=1/2+val_G(p)/8 and the argmax rule all confirmed; 512 of the 692 had val_G(p)=val_G(q), and in every one of those 512 the argmax over controlled vertices was {m_p, m_q}.

findings.defect: GAP: the algorithmic half is asserted, not proved, yet the result is filed as "proved". Missing statement, exactly: "There is a polynomial-time algorithm on the class of stopping SSGs that can be reduced to a single vertex by repeated contraction of parts with at most two exits and boundedly many entries, the parts and quotients being recursively of the same shape and of geometrically decreasing size." No definition of the class is given (what "recursively of the same shape" means is left open), no recursion for the running time is written down, and no member of the class is exhibited — so the standing test "is a member already inside thm:few-avg / thm:kacyclic / thm:bounded-components / thm:escape-class / thm:few-denominator / thm:modulator / min(m,k)=O(log N)?" cannot even be applied. What IS proved is the contraction step (thm:fs16-contract) and the boundary framing against rem:fold-width, which are sound.
findings.evidence: The LaTeX carries the claim only inside rem:fs16-two, with no theorem, no proof and no instance; the route's own verification line says "no separate implementation of the recursive algorithm was made". The reading of thm:fold as a three-exit part (exits u, t_0, t_1 on 6D+2 vertices, 2^D pieces) does check out against frontier.tex l.12368 and rem:fold-width l.3140.

findings.defect: The argument "a black-box composition multiplies the quantity to be resolved by at most O(s) while multiplying the size by at least s" is wrong for a general context: H<G> has |V_H| - c + c|G| vertices, where c is the number of CALLS, so the size multiplier relative to |G| is at least c, not at least s = |V_H|. With c much smaller than s the displayed reasoning yields only "the gap/size ratio improves by at most O(s/c)", not "by at most a constant factor". The conclusion is correct as stated for automata (c = s, the case of the theorem's application) and is not contradicted by measurement, but it is not proved for c < s.
findings.evidence: Hill-climbing over admissible contexts with a fixed number of calls (t_onecall.py, t_fewcall.py): with c=1 the steepest |dV/dp|(1/2) found is exactly 1 at every s = 1..9 (no growth in s); with c=2 it saturates near 1.52 up to s=9; with c=3 it reaches 2.01 at s=8 — consistent with steepness being governed by the number of calls, which is what the corollary needs and does not prove.

findings.defect: The verification claim "the derivative formula agrees EXACTLY with an exact rational secant at 185 of 203 contexts; the 18 exceptions are points where the optimal profile changes and the derivative is one-sided" misdescribes what was measured. A central secant with h = 10^{-6} equals the derivative exactly only when V is affine or quadratic in p on the interval; the statistic therefore measures the degree of V in p, not the validity of the formula, and the stated explanation of the exceptions is wrong (the exceptions can simply be the O(h^2) term).
findings.evidence: On the route's own ruin contexts, where there is no controlled vertex at all at p=q so the profile cannot change, the exact central secant differs from the exact derivative: s=3 gives secant 500000000000/250000000001 against dV/dp = 2 (difference 8e-12), s=5 gives 750000000001/250000000003 against 3, s=7 gives 250000000001000000000000/62500000001500000000001 against 4. The formula itself is fine: I verified dV/dp = sum_c N_c Delta_c against exact dual-number differentiation of the frozen linear system at 500 of 500 (context,p,q) points, with zero mismatches.

findings.defect: The JSON headline's "so 2^{Omega(a)} copies" conflates |V_H| with the number of copies: the theorem bounds |V_H| from below, and the number of plugged-in copies is the number of calls, which may be far smaller than |V_H|. The LaTeX states it correctly ("needs 2^{Omega(a)} vertices ... every finite-automaton verdict ... one call per state ... needs 2^{Omega(a)} states"), so only the summary is loose. Also "exactly two affine pieces" in thm:fs16-contract should be "at most two": when p_e = q_e the gate is a single affine map.
findings.evidence: Definition of composition in def:fs16-context; and p_e = q_e whenever the part has no controlled vertex, verified in the contraction runs.

findings.defect: "This is the one place in the paper where an algorithm the development actually uses rests on an unchecked citation" overstates what is repaired: def:simorder (l.10190-10193) itself says "Everything below uses only Z_0 subset {w*=0} and Z_1 subset {w*=1}, so any sound under-approximation may be substituted", so nothing in the paper is unsound because of the citation; what fs16:assure adds is exactness (hence strength) of M1's seed, proved inside the model. verdict:
NOT SOUND as stated: one major finding survives, plus six minor ones. Nothing is fatal — no claimed family, instance, number or identity failed to reproduce, and every "proved" statement I reconstructed is true; the major finding is a hypothesis that excludes the theorem's own advertised applications and its own tightness evidence, and it is repairable by a hypothesis change I verified.

WHAT IS SOLID. The mathematics of the six core results is correct and I could not break it. fs16:positive and fs16:assure: both fixed-point proofs reconstruct completely (the Min clause "both successors in Y", the average clause "both in W and some in Y", the rank-descent Max strategy, the c<1 escape argument for A subset Y(A)); 8400 random SSGs including 5082 non-stopping ones agree with brute-force values. fs16:gate: the payoff transfer (psi increasing -> p, psi decreasing -> q) and the fixed-point assembly are right, p and q are genuinely incomparable (1/0 at a Max vertex, 0/1 at a Min vertex, verified), and ~1500 honest compositions match. fs16:contract: correct, 1751 contractions match. fs16:cross: the martingale, its quadratic variation, the exact level-crossing integral 2b(1-b)|Delta| and Doob's upcrossing bound g_j E[U] <= min(a(1-W),W(1-a)) <= 1/4 with D <= U+1 all check; verified on thousands of random and biased games and on L_n, G_m, WD, CC, where it reproduces rem:fs16-blind's "total variation exactly 1". fs16:lip: the Green's-function formula agreed exactly with dual-number differentiation at 500 of 500 points and the bound was never violated (worst ratio 1/4). fs16:mixmin/mixmono and fs16:topctrl are correct as mathematics. No standing error of the project appears: no greedy policy iteration in a non-stopping game, no collapsing dict rows (the route accumulates; I checked the collapse case is Delta=0 anyway), no sink-index collisions, no pair-test-for-own-successor confusion (the route never uses a decision rule), no vacuous-stall claim, no unreachable-vertex separation, and the GAP and rem:fs16-scope are stated honestly.

THE MAJOR FINDING. def:fs16-context's admissibility reads calls as CONTROLLED vertices, which forbids every cycle through calls: an admissible all-call context is an acyclic automaton. So thm:fs16-noamp and thm:fs16-noqual, as stated, do not cover cyclic devices — not the birth-and-death counter that supplies every number in rem:fs16-measured (inadmissible for every s >= 2), not the route's own steepest 4-state automaton, and not "every finite-automaton verdict on a stream of independent plays", which the theorem's own statement claims. Worse, the tightness claim inverts inside the hypothesis: my exhaustive s<=4 search gives admissible maxima 1, 1, 5/4, 3/2 against 1, 4/3, 2, 12/5 overall, and the admissible time-expanded ruin's ratio to the bound falls from 0.25 to 0.022 as s goes 1 -> 121, so "the linear law is tight, not an artefact of the proof" is false for the class the theorem covers. The repair is one word and I verified it: use CHANCE-admissibility (calls read as average vertices; equivalently H^{1/2,1/2} stopping), under which H^{p,q} is stopping for every p,q in (0,1) — all that cor:fs16-lip and thm:fs16-noamp need, since delta <= 1/4 keeps the interval inside [1/4,3/4] — and under which 1893 compositions H<C_theta> with inadmissible H were all stopping with the gate values. Strong admissibility must remain in lem:fs16-gate itself (2-state ruin plus a one-vertex Max game gives a non-stopping H<G>). With that change the route's bottom line survives intact and then genuinely covers repeated play, counters and automata.

RECOMMENDATION TO THE ROOT AGENT. Integrate fs16:positive, fs16:assure, fs16:bias, fs16:gate, fs16:contract, fs16:cross and fs16:mixmin/mixmono as they stand (modulo the three one-line repairs: G/M stopping, the diagonal constant, "at most two pieces"). Restate thm:fs16-noamp and thm:fs16-noqual with chance-admissibility and rewrite rem:fs16-measured to say that the linear law is attained only by CYCLIC devices and that within the acyclic class the steepest devices measured are far below the bound (an honest open question worth recording: the maximum of dV/dp over chance-admissible contexts on s vertices, linear, versus over acyclic ones, apparently sublinear). Restate thm:fs16-topctrl with the epsilon-damped tie-break and O(a) added vertices. Demote fs16:two's algorithmic corollary to an explicitly-flagged GAP, or define the class and write the recursion. Fix the rem:fs16-checks sentence about the secant.
